Life expectancy keeps rising across most regions

Global life expectancy has climbed steadily for decades, according to new estimates published this week. Researchers say better sanitation, vaccines, and falling child mortality explain most of the gain.

The report notes that progress is uneven. Some regions added more than a decade of expected life since 1990, while others stalled because of conflict and underfunded health systems. Analysts caution that averages can hide wide gaps between countries and between income groups.

Public-health groups called for sustained investment in primary care and in data collection, arguing that reliable measurement is a prerequisite for planning. The full dataset and methodology notes are available from the research team.
